questions.q: What is the key distinction a capability map draws, per this lesson?
options: What an organization needs to be able to do, versus who does it or which tool implements it
Centralized versus decentralized operating models
Public versus private data classification
Free versus paid governance software
questions.explain: A capability map separates the 'what' (the capability) from implementation detail (who/which tool), per capability-based planning practice.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the eight capability domains listed in this lesson?
options: Lineage tracking
Marketing campaign management
Payroll processing
Office space planning
questions.explain: Lineage tracking is one of the eight domains: metadata, cataloging, lineage, classification, access control, quality, stewardship, audit.

questions.q: Per this lesson, can two organizations with the same capability gaps run completely different operating models?
options: Yes — the capability map is a different lens from the operating-model question
No, capability gaps and operating models are the same thing
No, only centralized organizations can have capability gaps
Yes, but only if they use the exact same software vendor
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states the capability map is a different lens than the operating-model question — they vary independently.

questions.q: Which capability domains does Chapter 3 (Metadata and Catalog Architecture) cover, per this lesson's mapping?
options: Metadata management, cataloging and discovery, and lineage tracking
Audit and monitoring only
Stewardship workflow only
Payroll and HR capabilities
questions.explain: The lesson maps capabilities 1-3 (metadata, cataloging, lineage) onto Chapter 3.

questions.q: According to the lesson, were data quality management and stewardship workflow re-taught in this course?
options: No — they were already covered at the practice level in Data Governance Foundations
Yes, they are the primary focus of Chapter 1
No, because they don't exist as governance capabilities
Yes, in a brand-new framework invented for this course
questions.explain: The lesson states quality and stewardship practice were already covered in Foundations and are treated here only as capabilities needing architecture support.
